# B-52 crashes at Edwards, killing 8

![](https://breakingdefense.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/13/2023/03/230309_b52_nuclear_6499975-scaled-e1722459652660-1024x575.jpg)

A US Air Force B-52H Stratofortress is pictured flying Jan. 6, 2021. (US Air Force photo by Staff Sgt. Stephanie Serrano)

**_UPDATED 6/16/2026 at 9:37 am ET with new information from a press conference at Edwards Air Force Base._**

WASHINGTON — A US Air Force [B-52 Stratofortress](https://breakingdefense.com/tag/b-52/) bomber crashed Monday after taking off from Edwards Air Force Base in California, killing eight people on board the aircraft, according to military authorities.

Col. James Hayes, deputy commander of the 412th Test Wing at Edwards, said in a briefing with reporters Monday that the crash was “unsurvivable.” A mixed crew of military and government contractors were aboard the bomber, according to Hayes.

Boeing, the prime contractor for the Stratofortress, said in a [statement](https://x.com/Boeing/status/2066683878757011590?s=20) Monday evening that two company employees were on board the B-52 that crashed.

“We extend our deepest condolences to the loved ones of the eight crew members who lost their lives” in the incident, the company said.

The crash occurred around 11:20 am local time, and Hayes said the aircraft was supporting a radar modernization program for the bomber. Edwards is located in the desert north of Los Angeles.

Officials are now investigating the cause of the crash, and a subsequent accident investigation board will determine what information can be released to the public, according to Hayes. The process could take “upwards of six months,” he said.

“It is with profound sadness that we mourn the loss of eight teammates today at Edwards AFB. My thoughts are with the bomber and test communities during this difficult time,” Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Kenneth Wilsbach said in a statement posted on X. “I am keeping the families, friends, and loved ones affected in my prayers.”

The B-52 is a long-range, swept-wing bomber that entered service in the 1950s. The Air Force is [upgrading](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/05/b-52-modernization-stabilized-after-cost-spikes-schedule-delays-air-force-official-says/) the bomber’s engines, radar and other subsystems to extend its service life into the 2050s. 

Edwards Air Force Base is a testing hub, where officials can evaluate upgrades and the integration of new weapons. Hayes said operations at the base will be suspended for the time being.

# 2026 United States Air Force Boeing B-52 crash

From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia

2026 United States Air Force Boeing B-52 crash

[![60-0061, the aircraft involved in the accident, at Edwards Air Force Base in 2025](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d5/B52H_60-0061.jpg/250px-B52H_60-0061.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:B52H_60-0061.jpg)

On June 15, 2026, a [United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force "United States Air Force") [Boeing B-52 Stratofortress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_B-52_Stratofortress "Boeing B-52 Stratofortress") [strategic bomber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategic_bomber "Strategic bomber") crashed shortly after takeoff near [Edwards Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwards_Air_Force_Base "Edwards Air Force Base") in [Edwards, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwards,_California "Edwards, California"), United States.[\[1\]](#cite_note-1)[\[2\]](#cite_note-2) All eight crew members were killed.[\[3\]](#cite_note-CNN-3)

The accident was the first crash of a B-52 since 2016, when one crashed at [Andersen Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andersen_Air_Force_Base "Andersen Air Force Base") in [Guam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guam "Guam"), injuring the seven crew members.[\[4\]](#cite_note-4)[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) It is also the deadliest crash of a B-52 since 1982, when one crashed at [Mather Air Force Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mather_Air_Force_Base "Mather Air Force Base") in [Sacramento County, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento_County,_California "Sacramento County, California"), killing all nine crew members.[\[6\]](#cite_note-6)

The aircraft involved in the accident was 60-0061, a [Boeing B-52H Stratofortress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing_B-52_Stratofortress#Variants "Boeing B-52 Stratofortress") operated by the [United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force "United States Air Force"), and assigned to the [412th Test Wing.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/412th_Test_Wing "412th Test Wing")[\[7\]](#cite_note-7) 60-0061 was operated by the [307th Bomb Wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/307th_Bomb_Wing "307th Bomb Wing") in the mid-2010s, where it was nicknamed _[The Spirit of Aggieland II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirit_of_Aggieland "Spirit of Aggieland")_.[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) In December 2025, Edwards Air Force Base said the aircraft had flown from [Port San Antonio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_San_Antonio "Port San Antonio") to the base after receiving an upgraded radar system as part of an ongoing modernization program.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9)

### Passengers and crew

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=2026_United_States_Air_Force_Boeing_B-52_crash&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Passengers and crew")\]

The aircraft was carrying eight people, including military personnel, civilians and contractors, on a routine test mission.[\[10\]](#cite_note-10)[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) [Boeing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boeing "Boeing") confirmed that two of its employees were among the occupants.[\[12\]](#cite_note-Sky-12)[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) The flight was intended to support an [active electronically scanned array](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Active_electronically_scanned_array "Active electronically scanned array") (AESA) radar modernization program.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)[\[15\]](#cite_note-15)

[![](//thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b4/B-52_Plane_Crash_Seen_From_Weather_Satellite_%28CIRA_2026-06-15_-_labels%29.gif/250px-B-52_Plane_Crash_Seen_From_Weather_Satellite_%28CIRA_2026-06-15_-_labels%29.gif?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:B-52_Plane_Crash_Seen_From_Weather_Satellite_\(CIRA_2026-06-15_-_labels\).gif)

The crash generated a large plume of smoke visible on satellite imagery ([CIRA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooperative_Institute_for_Research_in_the_Atmosphere "Cooperative Institute for Research in the Atmosphere") image pictured)

The crash was reported at 11:20 a.m. [PDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone").[\[16\]](#cite_note-16) Photos from the scene showed little recognizable wreckage after a post-crash fire, and video footage showed a large plume of black smoke rising from the crash site.[\[12\]](#cite_note-Sky-12)[\[17\]](#cite_note-17)

Shortly before 1:00 p.m., the base announced that the airfield was closed and all inbound aircraft were being diverted. All non-commercial visitor passes for the base were suspended in order to minimize interference with the emergency response.[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) The crash was later deemed "not survivable",[\[19\]](#cite_note-19) and [Air Force Materiel Command](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air_Force_Materiel_Command "Air Force Materiel Command") Commander Lieutenant general [Linda Hurry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_Hurry "Linda Hurry") confirmed the death of all 8 personnel on board the aircraft.[\[20\]](#cite_note-20) In a separate statement, [Chief of Staff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_of_Staff_of_the_United_States_Air_Force "Chief of Staff of the United States Air Force") of the Air Force General [Kenneth S. Wilsbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_S._Wilsbach "Kenneth S. Wilsbach") expressed his sorrows and thoughts with the bomber and testing community, saying that he is "keeping the families, friends, and loved ones affected in my prayers."[\[21\]](#cite_note-21)

The cause of the crash was not immediately known. [Colonel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonel_\(United_States\) "Colonel (United States)") James Hayes, Deputy Commander of the [412th Test Wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/412th_Test_Wing "412th Test Wing"), said the investigation could take an estimated six months.[\[22\]](#cite_note-22)

# Fact Check: Prayer Request For Baby Shot With Nail Gun Is NOT Current Or Verified -- Dates Back To 2010

 ![Fact Check: Prayer Request For Baby Shot With Nail Gun Is NOT Current Or Verified -- Dates Back To 2010](https://leadstories.com/assets_c/2022/08/screenshot_3479310-thumb-352xauto-3093349.jpg)Old Chain Mail

Did a 22-month-old baby accidentally shoot himself in the chest with a nail gun and is this child in critical condition? No, that's not true: This copy/paste chain letter dates back to 2010, and there is no evidence that this specific prayer request was ever based on a real incident. Some copies of the message have slightly different details and the name of the mother has been changed or the name of a person forwarding the message added as if they were a close acquaintance of the family, but the structure of the message is the same.

The viral prayer request has circulated on social media since 2010. Snopes.com [published an article](https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/prayer-request-child-shot-nail-gun/) about it on August 10, 2010. This article has been updated several times over the years to add details about additional variations. Most recently, the message was [posted on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/towtalley/posts/pfbid033iuaaJdYtwV62HEdDZduevnQ8hUY48n2726n3YVBKnwfzjzbWkgDyhQU7Nmmtbuzl) on August 1, 2022. The text reads:

> PRAYERS NEEDED :Urgent prayer request! Kayla Scott's 22 month old son accidentally shot himself in the chest with a brad nailer (construction nail gun). It went off in his heart ~ He is now in critical condition and not doing well neither is his mom ~ Please start a prayer chain for this baby Please copy & re-post. As you would want someone to do it for you, thanx guys I wanna see this as your status for at least half hr please!!!! COME ON PRAYER  
> A WARRIORS IN THE NAME OF JESUS 🙏💕🙏 A friend of a friend baby, 🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻

This is how the post appeared at the time of writing:  
[![nailgunpost01.jpg](https://leadstories.com/assets_c/2022/08/nailgunpost01-thumb-700x307-3093425.jpg)](https://leadstories.com/nailgunpost01.jpg)  
_(Image source: Facebook screenshot taken on Wed Aug 03 14:15:58 2022 UTC)_

Many copies of the original forward-date from mid-October in 2010. Examples of the text circulating at that time ([here](https://www.facebook.com/delphine.hammond/posts/pfbid0BEDjwMASQD1BcvRbUXHb3CrqcQYgvv1CzptuRtXzgrRPUKTwMtXuv2ULDmZigh3hl) and [here](https://www.facebook.com/tweetygal1972/posts/pfbid0319Q45ckz7iCLSycVsAE5gX3j3nUE2yaYrzXaaZmXhqVxj7DETCr4xEfsB241GoKRl)) were almost identical to the text circulating now:

> PRAYERS NEEDED!! URGENT PRAYER REQUEST!!! PLEASE RE-POST!! KAYLA SCOTT'S 22 MONTH OLD SON SHOT HIMSELF IN THE CHEST WITH A BRAD NAILER~ IT WENT IN HIS HEART~ HE IS NOW IN CRITICAL CONDITION AND NOT DOING WELL ~ NEITHER IS HIS MOM ~PLEASE START A PRAYER CHAIN FOR THIS BABY~ PLEASE COPY &... REPOST AS YOU WOULD WANT SOMEONE TO DO IT FOR YOU!

[![nailgunpost02.jpg](https://leadstories.com/assets_c/2022/08/nailgunpost02-thumb-700xauto-3093427.jpg)](https://leadstories.com/nailgunpost02.jpg)

The claim has been debunked several times over the years. In August 2016 [truthorfiction.com](https://www.truthorfiction.com/prayer-request-kayla-scotts-22-month-old-son-shot-self-with-brad-nailer/) and [thatsnonsense.com](https://www.thatsnonsense.com/kayla-scott-never-ending-prayer-request/) published articles that highlighted that after circulating for that length of time the nature of the claim had evolved from simply unverified to outdated as well. News Channel 3 in Kalamazoo, Michigan [ran a segment](https://wwmt.com/news/local/child-shot-by-nail-gun-facebook-post-is-a-hoax) about the prayer request on April 29, 2019. By that point it was considered a hoax.

# Kayla Scott’s 22-Month-old Son Shot Self with Brad Nailer-Outdated! – Truth or Fiction?

**Prayer Request: Kayla Scott’s 22-Month-old Son Shot Self with Brad Nailer-Outdated!**

**Summary of eRumor:**  
A prayer request is making the rounds on Facebook for the 22-month-old son of a woman named Kayla Scott who shot himself in the heart with a nail gun and is in critical condition.  
**The Truth:**  
This prayer request has been circulating social media since 2010, so we’re classifying it as “outdated.”  
One of the earliest versions of [the story appeared in a DIY chat](http://www.diychatroom.com/f29/just-reminder-unplug-power-tools-78015/) room in August 2010. In that version, the poster said “a local 22-month-old boy” had picked up his dad’s electric brad gun and shot himself in the chest, just below the sternum. The post wasn’t a prayer request, but rather a reminder to unplug power tools when not in use:

If you own an electric powered brad nailer, as I do, PLEASE remember to unplug it when you are not using it–even for a minute. A local 22 month old boy picked up his Dad’s, which was plugged in and turned ON and shot himself in the chest. The brad nail went just to the left of the Sternum, below the skin line and is into his heart. He is in critical condition at this time and the local Dr.’s here, which do heart surgery, are considering flying him to another hospital for surgery. Just one second in this child’s life is all that it took. Thanks for reading, David

![Screen Shot 2016-08-12 at 11.29.31 AM](https://www.truthorfiction.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/08/Screen-Shot-2016-08-12-at-11.29.31-AM-358x142.png)

That story is impossible to fact-check since it doesn’t name the boy or the city that the accident supposedly happened in.  
Two months later, in October 2010, the story made its way to Facebook in the form of a payer request. In that version, the boy’s mother had a name, Kayla Scott:

When the prayer request for Kayla Scott [made its way to a prayer forum hosted by SingSnap](http://www.singsnap.com/karaoke/forum/topic/bc248c5) that same month, questions began to surface about whether or not the story was true. Skeptics noted that the story had been in circulation for months, and nobody had actually heard from Scott or her injured son’s family.  
It should also be noted that different names have been associated with the story of the years, too. The boy’s mother has had numerous names — including Dedee Parsons, Teresa Lynch and Cheryl Dewitts — none of which have been confirmed.  
We also couldn’t find any news reports about a 22-month-old boy being shot in the chest with a brad nailer. There were reports of teens in [Hawaii](http://www.hawaiinewsnow.com/story/6186868/teen-survives-being-shot-in-the-heart-with-a-3-inch-nail) and [Michigan](http://www.medscape.com/viewarticle/785769) being shot in the heart with nail guns (both survived), but those stories don’t match the particulars of the Kayla Scott Prayer request.  
In the end, we can’t definitively prove that the story of the 22-month-old boy who shot himself in the chest with a brad nailer is false. But the prayer request is definitely outdated.

# Fact Check: Prayer Request For Baby Shot With Nail Gun Is NOT Current Or Verified -- Dates Back To 2010

 ![Fact Check: Prayer Request For Baby Shot With Nail Gun Is NOT Current Or Verified -- Dates Back To 2010](https://leadstories.com/assets_c/2022/08/xscreenshot_3479310-thumb-352xauto-3093349.jpg.pagespeed.ic.nXwi_cCqXo.webp)Old Chain Mail

Did a 22-month-old baby accidentally shoot himself in the chest with a nail gun and is this child in critical condition? No, that's not true: This copy/paste chain letter dates back to 2010, and there is no evidence that this specific prayer request was ever based on a real incident. Some copies of the message have slightly different details and the name of the mother has been changed or the name of a person forwarding the message added as if they were a close acquaintance of the family, but the structure of the message is the same.

The viral prayer request has circulated on social media since 2010. Snopes.com [published an article](https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/prayer-request-child-shot-nail-gun/) about it on August 10, 2010. This article has been updated several times over the years to add details about additional variations. Most recently, the message was [posted on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/towtalley/posts/pfbid033iuaaJdYtwV62HEdDZduevnQ8hUY48n2726n3YVBKnwfzjzbWkgDyhQU7Nmmtbuzl) on August 1, 2022. The text reads:

> PRAYERS NEEDED :Urgent prayer request! Kayla Scott's 22 month old son accidentally shot himself in the chest with a brad nailer (construction nail gun). It went off in his heart ~ He is now in critical condition and not doing well neither is his mom ~ Please start a prayer chain for this baby Please copy & re-post. As you would want someone to do it for you, thanx guys I wanna see this as your status for at least half hr please!!!! COME ON PRAYER  
> A WARRIORS IN THE NAME OF JESUS 🙏💕🙏 A friend of a friend baby, 🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻

This is how the post appeared at the time of writing:  
[![nailgunpost01.jpg](https://leadstories.com/assets_c/2022/08/xnailgunpost01-thumb-700x307-3093425.jpg.pagespeed.ic.wCWp6EL37r.webp)](https://leadstories.com/nailgunpost01.jpg)  
_(Image source: Facebook screenshot taken on Wed Aug 03 14:15:58 2022 UTC)_

Many copies of the original forward-date from mid-October in 2010. Examples of the text circulating at that time ([here](https://www.facebook.com/delphine.hammond/posts/pfbid0BEDjwMASQD1BcvRbUXHb3CrqcQYgvv1CzptuRtXzgrRPUKTwMtXuv2ULDmZigh3hl) and [here](https://www.facebook.com/tweetygal1972/posts/pfbid0319Q45ckz7iCLSycVsAE5gX3j3nUE2yaYrzXaaZmXhqVxj7DETCr4xEfsB241GoKRl)) were almost identical to the text circulating now:

> PRAYERS NEEDED!! URGENT PRAYER REQUEST!!! PLEASE RE-POST!! KAYLA SCOTT'S 22 MONTH OLD SON SHOT HIMSELF IN THE CHEST WITH A BRAD NAILER~ IT WENT IN HIS HEART~ HE IS NOW IN CRITICAL CONDITION AND NOT DOING WELL ~ NEITHER IS HIS MOM ~PLEASE START A PRAYER CHAIN FOR THIS BABY~ PLEASE COPY &... REPOST AS YOU WOULD WANT SOMEONE TO DO IT FOR YOU!

[![nailgunpost02.jpg](https://leadstories.com/assets_c/2022/08/xnailgunpost02-thumb-700xauto-3093427.jpg.pagespeed.ic.bBlsx1Kixt.webp)](https://leadstories.com/nailgunpost02.jpg)

The claim has been debunked several times over the years. In August 2016 [truthorfiction.com](https://www.truthorfiction.com/prayer-request-kayla-scotts-22-month-old-son-shot-self-with-brad-nailer/) and [thatsnonsense.com](https://www.thatsnonsense.com/kayla-scott-never-ending-prayer-request/) published articles that highlighted that after circulating for that length of time the nature of the claim had evolved from simply unverified to outdated as well. News Channel 3 in Kalamazoo, Michigan [ran a segment](https://wwmt.com/news/local/child-shot-by-nail-gun-facebook-post-is-a-hoax) about the prayer request on April 29, 2019. By that point it was considered a hoax.

# Kayla Scott’s 22-Month-old Son Shot Self with Brad Nailer-Outdated! – Truth or Fiction?

**Prayer Request: Kayla Scott’s 22-Month-old Son Shot Self with Brad Nailer-Outdated!**

**Summary of eRumor:**  
A prayer request is making the rounds on Facebook for the 22-month-old son of a woman named Kayla Scott who shot himself in the heart with a nail gun and is in critical condition.  
**The Truth:**  
This prayer request has been circulating social media since 2010, so we’re classifying it as “outdated.”  
One of the earliest versions of [the story appeared in a DIY chat](http://www.diychatroom.com/f29/just-reminder-unplug-power-tools-78015/) room in August 2010. In that version, the poster said “a local 22-month-old boy” had picked up his dad’s electric brad gun and shot himself in the chest, just below the sternum. The post wasn’t a prayer request, but rather a reminder to unplug power tools when not in use:

If you own an electric powered brad nailer, as I do, PLEASE remember to unplug it when you are not using it–even for a minute. A local 22 month old boy picked up his Dad’s, which was plugged in and turned ON and shot himself in the chest. The brad nail went just to the left of the Sternum, below the skin line and is into his heart. He is in critical condition at this time and the local Dr.’s here, which do heart surgery, are considering flying him to another hospital for surgery. Just one second in this child’s life is all that it took. Thanks for reading, David

![Screen Shot 2016-08-12 at 11.29.31 AM](https://www.truthorfiction.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/08/Screen-Shot-2016-08-12-at-11.29.31-AM-358x142.png)

That story is impossible to fact-check since it doesn’t name the boy or the city that the accident supposedly happened in.  
Two months later, in October 2010, the story made its way to Facebook in the form of a payer request. In that version, the boy’s mother had a name, Kayla Scott:

When the prayer request for Kayla Scott [made its way to a prayer forum hosted by SingSnap](http://www.singsnap.com/karaoke/forum/topic/bc248c5) that same month, questions began to surface about whether or not the story was true. Skeptics noted that the story had been in circulation for months, and nobody had actually heard from Scott or her injured son’s family.  
It should also be noted that different names have been associated with the story of the years, too. The boy’s mother has had numerous names — including Dedee Parsons, Teresa Lynch and Cheryl Dewitts — none of which have been confirmed.  
We also couldn’t find any news reports about a 22-month-old boy being shot in the chest with a brad nailer. There were reports of teens in [Hawaii](http://www.hawaiinewsnow.com/story/6186868/teen-survives-being-shot-in-the-heart-with-a-3-inch-nail) and [Michigan](http://www.medscape.com/viewarticle/785769) being shot in the heart with nail guns (both survived), but those stories don’t match the particulars of the Kayla Scott Prayer request.  
In the end, we can’t definitively prove that the story of the 22-month-old boy who shot himself in the chest with a brad nailer is false. But the prayer request is definitely outdated.

# Scam alert: Don’t fall for the ‘Child shot by nail gun’ hoax on Facebook

You are here: [Home](https://www.ricksdailytips.com/) / [Scam alerts](https://www.ricksdailytips.com/category/scams/) / Scam alert: Don’t fall for the ‘Child shot by nail gun’ hoax on Facebook

![](https://www.ricksdailytips.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/nail-gun-hoax.png)Want to get my easy to follow Tech Tips in your email?

Sign up for my daily [**Rick’s Tech Tips Newsletter**](https://www.ricksdailytips.com/daily-updates-newsletter/)!

* * *

It’s no secret that scammers love plying their trade on social media, and Facebook is far and away their favorite venue.

Facebook scams and hoaxes come and go, but some of the most insidious ones keep popping up on a recurring basis. One of the worst hoaxes of them all has been making the rounds [**for well over a decade**](https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/prayer-request-child-shot-nail-gun/), and unfortunately it’s back yet again. 

This hoax claims that a young 22 month old boy shot himself in the chest with a brad nail gun and he is struggling to survive. The hoaxster asks the reader to pray for the child and “copy and paste” the info on their Timeline.

The actual text of this particular hoax varies a bit from time to time, but this is the version that is going around right now:

“_PRAYERS NEEDED: Urgent prayer request! The Scott’s (From Antioch Baptist Church) 22-month-old son accidentally shot himself in the chest with a brad nailer (construction nail gun). It went off in his heart ~ He is now in critical condition and not doing well, and neither is his mom ~ Please start a prayer chain for this baby. Please copy & re-post. As you would want someone to do it for you, thanks, guys. I wanna see this as your status for at least half hr, please!!!! A good friend just posted, asking all prayer warriors to start their own chain by copy-and-posting, and I don’t ask often, but this is just a baby._  
_This is a copy & paste._“

While there’s absolutely nothing wrong with praying, it’s important to resist the urge to copy and paste this hoax onto your own Timeline because that just incentivizes the scammer to keep creating new hoaxes.

Let me say again, there is absolutely nothing wrong with praying for someone. If you (or one of your friends) knows first-hand of someone that’s in need of prayer, by all means share that info on your Timeline. The same goes for someone you see mentioned in a reputable news source that needs prayer.

However, if you see a request for prayer for a stranger that asks you to copy and paste it into a post of your own, you can rest assured that it’s a hoax.

I really hate these hoax prayer requests because they tug at the heart strings of innocent readers while also making it easy to miss legitimate prayer requests due to all the digital noise created by the hoaxes. I wish the scammers would get a job and leave innocent folks alone, but that’s highly unlikely to happen in today’s world.

# Kayla Scott’s 22-Month-old Son Shot Self with Brad Nailer-Outdated! – Truth or Fiction?

**Prayer Request: Kayla Scott’s 22-Month-old Son Shot Self with Brad Nailer-Outdated!**

**Summary of eRumor:**  
A prayer request is making the rounds on Facebook for the 22-month-old son of a woman named Kayla Scott who shot himself in the heart with a nail gun and is in critical condition.  
**The Truth:**  
This prayer request has been circulating social media since 2010, so we’re classifying it as “outdated.”  
One of the earliest versions of [the story appeared in a DIY chat](http://www.diychatroom.com/f29/just-reminder-unplug-power-tools-78015/) room in August 2010. In that version, the poster said “a local 22-month-old boy” had picked up his dad’s electric brad gun and shot himself in the chest, just below the sternum. The post wasn’t a prayer request, but rather a reminder to unplug power tools when not in use:

If you own an electric powered brad nailer, as I do, PLEASE remember to unplug it when you are not using it–even for a minute. A local 22 month old boy picked up his Dad’s, which was plugged in and turned ON and shot himself in the chest. The brad nail went just to the left of the Sternum, below the skin line and is into his heart. He is in critical condition at this time and the local Dr.’s here, which do heart surgery, are considering flying him to another hospital for surgery. Just one second in this child’s life is all that it took. Thanks for reading, David

![Screen Shot 2016-08-12 at 11.29.31 AM](https://www.truthorfiction.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/08/Screen-Shot-2016-08-12-at-11.29.31-AM-358x142.png)

That story is impossible to fact-check since it doesn’t name the boy or the city that the accident supposedly happened in.  
Two months later, in October 2010, the story made its way to Facebook in the form of a payer request. In that version, the boy’s mother had a name, Kayla Scott:

When the prayer request for Kayla Scott [made its way to a prayer forum hosted by SingSnap](http://www.singsnap.com/karaoke/forum/topic/bc248c5) that same month, questions began to surface about whether or not the story was true. Skeptics noted that the story had been in circulation for months, and nobody had actually heard from Scott or her injured son’s family.  
It should also be noted that different names have been associated with the story of the years, too. The boy’s mother has had numerous names — including Dedee Parsons, Teresa Lynch and Cheryl Dewitts — none of which have been confirmed.  
We also couldn’t find any news reports about a 22-month-old boy being shot in the chest with a brad nailer. There were reports of teens in [Hawaii](http://www.hawaiinewsnow.com/story/6186868/teen-survives-being-shot-in-the-heart-with-a-3-inch-nail) and [Michigan](http://www.medscape.com/viewarticle/785769) being shot in the heart with nail guns (both survived), but those stories don’t match the particulars of the Kayla Scott Prayer request.  
In the end, we can’t definitively prove that the story of the 22-month-old boy who shot himself in the chest with a brad nailer is false. But the prayer request is definitely outdated.

### https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/features/drm
# Steam DRM (Steamworks Documentation)

## Overview

The Steam DRM wrapper is an important part of Steam platform because it verifies game ownership and ensures that Steamworks features work properly by launching Steam before launching the game.

The Steam DRM wrapper by itself is not an anti-piracy solution. The Steam DRM wrapper protects against extremely casual piracy (i.e. copying all game files to another computer) and has some obfuscation, but it is easily removed by a motivated attacker.

We suggest enhancing the value of legitimate copies of your game by using Steamworks features which won't work on non-legitimate copies (e.g. online multiplayer, achievements, leaderboards, trading cards, etc.).

See [Using the Steam Wrapper with Other DRM](#other_drm) for more information on combining the Steam DRM wrapper with other DRM or anti-tampering solutions.

## Automated Steam DRM Wrapper

The Steam wrapper can be applied from within your SteamPipe upload script. This performs an initialization request to the Steam servers via the logged in client, then posts your plaintext executable to the Steam back end via HTTP. The wrap is performed server side, and then steamcmd downloads the wrapped executable.

To perform a DRM wrap with SteamPipe, have your script login and then run the drm\_wrap Steam command:

drm\_wrap \[appid\] \[input filename\] \[output filename\] \[toolname\] \[flags\]

Parameters:

*   **appid** - Your numeric application ID  
    
*   **input filename** - Relative or absolute path to input plaintext executable. Remember to quote paths that may contain spaces!  
    
*   **output filename** - Relative or absolute path where the tool will write the output wrapped executable.  
    
*   **toolname** - "drmtoolp" is currently the only supported toolname parameter.  
    
*   **flags** - Bitmask of the following numeric flags specifying tool behavior.  
    *   **0** - Normal wrap (most protection)  
        
    *   **6** - Compatibility mode (disables obfuscation)  
        
    *   **32** - Skip debugger check  
        
    *   **38** - compatibility mode and also skip debugger check (least protection)

Example run\_build.bat script to login, apply DRM, build and upload the build to Steam (where App ID is 480):

builder\\steamcmd.exe +login mysteamaccount +drm\_wrap 480 "D:\\src\\steamworkssdk\\steamworksexample\\release\\steamworksexample.exe" "D:\\src\\steamworkssdk\\tools\\ContentBuilder\\content\\windows\_content\\SteamworksExample.exe" drmtoolp 0 +run\_app\_build ..\\scripts\\app\_build\_480.vdf +quit

## Manual Steam DRM Wrapper

To quickly wrap an exe with the Steam wrapper use the Steamworks App Data Admin page to wrap the primary game exe.

1.  Select the game you want to add DRM to on your App Admin page  
    
2.  Select Edit Steamworks Settings in the Technical Tools Section of the App Admin page  
    
3.  From the Security Tab, select DRM.  
    
4.  Upload the primary game exe - See the automated wrapper section above for more information on the tool execution options.  
    
5.  Download the exe back to your local machine  
    
6.  Rename the exe back to the original name  
    
7.  Copy it to the source location for your Content Tool depots  
    
8.  Build a new version of your depot  
    
9.  Test that depot on your local content server

## Using the Steam Wrapper with Other DRM

The Steam wrapper can and should be used in combination with other DRM solutions. To do so, apply the Steam wrapper in compatibility mode first before applying any other DRM. Apply it first so that it does not interfere with the DRM solution. Compatibility mode will disable DRM capabilities of the wrapper.

Submit the exe in compatibility mode by either selecting it in the drop down on the Steamworks page or using the appropriate flags in the automated drmtool.

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q. My C# / .Net game doesn't run after applying the Steam wrapper**  
**A.** The Steam wrapper doesn't support .Net applications. Instead of using the DRM wrapper, use [SteamAPI\_RestartAppIfNecessary](https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/sdk/api#SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary).

**Q. My game doesn't run after applying the Steam DRM wrapper**  
**A.** The Steam wrapper can break other DRM tools. See [Using the Steam Wrapper with Other DRM](#other_drm), as there may be a conflict.

**Q. Do I need to apply DRM to my exe every time I make a new build?**  
**A.** Yes, each build you intend to publish needs to be wrapped with the Steam wrapper. Try automating it using the Automated Steam Wrapper process documented above.

**Q. An Anti-virus vendor has detected my binary as having a virus after applying the Steam DRM wrapper. What can I do?**  
**A.** False positives like this can happen, as the DRM injection process is modifying your binary in the same way a virus might do. Feel free to contact the vendor, or use the API instead of the Steam DRM wrapper.

### https://www.pcgamesn.com/steam-offline-mode-designed-be-indefinite-valve-are-working-make-it-more-robust
# Steam Offline Mode "is designed to be indefinite." Valve are working to make it "more robust"

**Edit: Valve's man has returned to the [June thread](http://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/864969953572102601/#c864969953730401285) his comments were sourced from to provide a slightly bewildered update. "Holy thread necro," he wrote. "****The 'two week' timeout issue has been fixed for months now, along with several other bugs. We're still working on improvements, and you might catch them if you read the patch notes carefully, but we don't bother to post on the forums every time we fix something."**

**Righto. Original story follows.**

Valve have shed a little light on how Steam's Offline Mode works and how they're working to improve it. One of the developer's programmers, Henry Goffin, took to Steam's forums to answer a question about how the client's offline mode is supposed to work: "\[it's\] designed to be indefinite," he wrote. "You can't access any of Steam's online features such as friends lists or saved game synchronization, of course, but the client should allow you to run in Offline Mode for as long as you like."

Since the client's launch back in 2004 users have come across bugs with the feature and being able to play your games without an internet connection has never been a guarantee. According to Goffin, the developer's been working on improvements that will go live "some day soon".

The comments spun out from [a thread](http://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/864969953572102601/) discussing the reliability of Steam's offline mode. MatTheCat complained that when he worked offshore for a five week stretch he'd find himself locked out from Steam, despite being in Offline Mode, and unable to access his game.

[User Facedown replied](http://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/864969953572102601/#c864969953589725150), saying "Off-line mode is designed to reset about every two weeks at which time you are supposed to go online again." This is what spurred Goffin to weigh in, [saying](http://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/864969953572102601/#c864969953730401285):

"This is not actually true - Offline Mode is designed to be indefinite. You can't access any of Steam's online features such as friends lists or saved game synchronization, of course, but the client should allow you to run in Offline Mode for as long as you like.

"That said, there are many components involved in Offline Mode, and some of them have known issues and bugs which we are continually working to improve. We're aware that it doesn't always work as flawlessly as we want it to, but please keep reporting bugs with Offline Mode. It is not broken 'by design'."

[Later in the thread](http://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/864969953572102601/#c864969953745925033) he adds that Valve "have been working very hard on upgrading the underlying technology in Steam. We have no community managers or PR people, so all the time that we spend on forums is taking away from development time. That said, I know that it's frustrating to get no response, and it looks like we aren't doing anything about it."

The good news from all this is that the developer is actually working on something that should substantially improve Offline Mode:

"Many of the older games on Steam were using an older authentication system which has many known issues with Offline Mode and is incredibly difficult to maintain - it was written for a time when there were dozens of games on Steam, not thousands," explains Goffin. "We are in the process of upgrading every game in the Steam catalog to a newer authentication system (and fixing bugs that result from the conversion), but this is a slow and time-consuming process. Some day soon, once this work is completed, we will eliminate the old authentication system (represented by the ClientRegistry.blob file) and Offline Mode should immediately become much more robust."

Of course, "some day soon" in Valve terms is difficult to quantify but the developer is at least aware of and working on the problem.

_Earlier this evening I wrote a similar version of this post but it took a much more antagonistic tone and presented the facts of this story as something they shouldn't have been. This version better reflects Goffin's comments._

Nuance: some individual games add third-party DRM (e.g. Denuvo) that may require periodic online checks, and Steam offline has had bugs, but that is not a Steam-enforced 30-day license check. GOG installers being DRM-free/forever is broadly correct.

samples.research:
The tweet claims Steam itself enforces DRM via mandatory 30-day reauthentication, such that 'your games will break in 30 days once Steam goes down,' contrasted with GOG backups working forever. This claim is contested and partially misleading.

Supporting the tweet's premise: Many users report time-limited offline mode. A 2013 Steam forum user reported "So there is some sort of time limited DRM on steam offline mode, and it will stop working after about 2 weeks" (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/828937979095845728). Another forum thread describes "The Steam Offline Mode requires being re-logged in and validated on a regular basis (something like once every 30 days or so), you cant just set it offline and be good, it will eventualy fail and require re-authentication" (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/0/1700542332330146872). Current guides (2026) similarly state users can typically play "approximately 14 to 30 days before the client requires a re-authentication handshake" (https://gamewiki.blog/what-happens-if-i-play-steam-games-offline).

However, Valve's own official position directly contradicts the tweet's framing that this is Steam enforcing DRM by design. A Valve employee stated on the Steam forums: "This is not actually true - Offline Mode is designed to be indefinite... That said, there are many components involved in Offline Mode, and some of them have known issues and bugs which we are continually working to improve... It is not broken 'by design.'" and noted "The 'two week' timeout issue has been fixed for months now, along with several other bugs" (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/864969953572102601). This was also reported by Blue's News: "A response from Valve to a thread about offline mode on Steam indicates that the way offline mode currently requires users to go online periodically... is a bug, and not working as intended" (https://www.bluesnews.com/cgi-bin/board.pl?action=viewthread&boardid=1&threadid=146408).

Crucially, much of the real-world lockout behavior users experience is attributable to third-party DRM (especially Denuvo) layered onto specific games by publishers, not Steam's core platform. One forum user explained: "If you have games with Denuvo or other DRM, of launchers, they will ask to phone home every period (like 30 days)" (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/0/587308261888419215/). Another user directly addressed the 'Steam is secretly like Denuvo' argument: "There isn't any compulsory DRM in Steam. It's the publisher/developer's choice whether they want to implement it or not... it allows to play offline indefinitely and backup and reinstall your whole library at will while offline at all times" and added "All games using Valve's DRM allow offline play indefinitely since 2013" (https://steamcommunity.com/app/359870/discussions/0/1850323802590261402). A 2026 Notebookcheck report confirms Denuvo (third-party), not Steam, is tightening restrictions: "A hypervisor bypass developer discovered Denuvo now asks players to authenticate tokens online every 14 days" and "Many Steam games, besides NBA 2K26, already penalize offline players" due to Denuvo specifically (https://www.notebookcheck.net/Denuvo-bolsters-DRM-in-Steam-games-even-as-hypervisor-achieves-piracy-milestone.1283939.0.html).

Also, Valve's Steamworks DRM (when publishers opt in) is distinguishable from third-party DRM like Denuvo, and developers can use Steamworks services without enabling Steam's own DRM at all, undercutting the tweet's claim that Steam 'enforces their own DRM' universally.

In short: the empirical behavior many users observe (games failing after ~2-4 weeks offline) is real and documented, but it is predominantly driven by third-party DRM (Denuvo) that publishers choose to add, exactly as the quoted post states ('If a game has DRM, that is a developer/publisher decision'). Valve has stated Steam's own offline mode is designed/intended to be indefinite, contradicting the tweet's framing that Steam itself mandates a 30-day reauthentication that will inevitably break all games. The tweet overgeneralizes a real but inconsistent, largely third-party-DRM-driven phenomenon as an official, universal Steam-enforced 30-day DRM rule, which misrepresents the distinction the quoted post was making.

# How to have reliable offline mode on Steam. :: Help and Tips

How to have reliable offline mode on Steam.

First off, I despise being forced to use Steam or indeed any other kind of invasive 3rd party middle man DRM, but since I have been gifted some free games and have also been stupid enough to pay for a few games that require Steam, I guess I am stuck with it, at least asd far as those games are concerned.

I work offshore. I am offshore for 5 weeks at a time. When I go offshore, I take my gaming laptop with me, which I like to play games on. Because I have no internet connection when I am offshore, I set all the invasive and defiling DRMs such as Origin and Steam to "OFFLINE MODE". Yet with Steam, even though I opt to log in in "OFFLINE MODE", after just a week or so, the Steam client tells me "There is no records of this username on your computer, please enter your username and password" With no internet connection, this is a pretty hard thing to do.

So my question is, if anyone would be so kind as to answer it, how do I make Steam go into a geniune offline mode, whereby I really don't need an internet connections to access my games.

I make no aopologies for the sour tone of my post. When Steam locked me out of my games that were meant to keep me amused for 5 weeks, rendering my gaming laptop an 8Kg weight around my neck, I was spitting bloody venom!

# Denuvo bolsters DRM in Steam games, even as hypervisor achieves piracy milestone

[![Banner for NBA 2K26 and Denuvo is shown](fileadmin/_processed_/d/2/csm_NBA2K26Denuvo_5238bf923b.jpg)

ⓘ 2K Games, Irdeto

](fileadmin/Notebooks/News/_nc5/NBA2K26Denuvo.jpg "Banner for NBA 2K26 and Denuvo is shown")

Banner for NBA 2K26 and Denuvo is shown

Staying offline indefinitely may no longer be an option with more Steam games. A hypervisor bypass developer discovered Denuvo now asks players to authenticate tokens online every 14 days. 2K Games titles like NBA 2K26 and Marvel’s Midnight Suns have the more restrictive DRM.

The hypervisor bypass has overcome the protection in every [Denuvo game](Decoding-Denuvo-s-impact-How-DRM-shields-early-game-revenue-by-up-to-20-percent.901313.0.html). Regardless, Irdeto seems intent on strengthening its [anti-piracy DRM](Latest-PlayStation-update-adds-problematic-DRM-to-some-digital-games.1282859.0.html). Andreh, a developer for the bypass noted how several 2K Games releases, including [_NBA 2K26_](Surprising-new-AAA-Xbox-Game-Pass-game-is-not-a-Microsoft-April-Fools-joke.1264336.0.html), now force more frequent online checks. If gamers remain offline for 14 days, the activation token will expire, blocking titles from booting.

## 2K Games introduces an updated Denuvo

On social media, [Pirat\_Nation](https://x.com/Pirat_Nation/status/2048372016726880723) addressed a recent Discord post from Andreh. He reveals that [_Marvel’s Midnight Suns_](Marvel-s-Midnight-Suns-confirmed-for-an-October-7-release-on-PC-and-consoles.626953.0.html) also has the more restrictive version of Denuvo. In the coming days, players may discover that other [Steam games](Valve-is-reportedly-planning-to-add-a-30-day-price-history-for-Steam-games.1274375.0.html) have the same requirements.

When installing titles, the DRM stores a unique activation token on each buyer’s system. Revisions to a PC’s configuration may prompt additional online re-authentication. Also, there is often a finite number of times tweaks are allowed before suffering a 24-hour lockout. [_Pragmata_ fans on Linux](Denuvo-blocks-Pragmata-Steam-Deck-and-Linux-players-as-reviews-slam-anti-piracy-DRM.1276439.0.html) experienced this when new Proton versions counted against a 5-machine limit.

Many Steam games, besides _NBA 2K26_, already penalize [offline players](Physical-Crimson-Desert-PS5-version-requires-48GB-release-date-download-to-play-offline.1249068.0.html). Still, in an effort to combat piracy, Irdeto has made it even harder to enjoy purchased content. Previously, in many cases, gamers could stay offline for months or longer if they did not update their hardware. Now, regardless of any changes, they must access internet connectivity more regularly.

## Irdeto is losing the battle against piracy

Despite Irdeto pledging to counter the hypervisor bypass, their latest efforts will have no impact. A virtualization layer tricks the DRM into authenticating a system. In a victory celebrated by the hacking community, [The Gamer](https://www.thegamer.com/there-are-no-more-remaining-uncracked-denuvo-games/) discussed how there no uncracked Denuvo games left. That said, some skeptics are wary of disabling Windows security settings to implement the bypass.

Instead of troubling pirates, the 14-day restriction could pose problems for legitimate buyers. Andreh explains how individuals without a reliable internet connection are most affected.

Expiring activation tokens aren’t the only concern for Denuvo opponents. Constant verification checks during gameplay can increase CPU usage. [_Resident Evil Requiem_](Resident-Evil-Requiem-performance-boosted-by-Denuvo-crack-as-piracy-threatens-DRM.1272150.0.html) is among several examples that see improved performance without the anti-piracy measure.

The tweet claims Steam itself enforces DRM via mandatory 30-day reauthentication, such that 'your games will break in 30 days once Steam goes down,' contrasted with GOG backups working forever. This claim is contested and partially misleading.

Supporting the tweet's premise: Many users report time-limited offline mode. A 2013 Steam forum user reported "So there is some sort of time limited DRM on steam offline mode, and it will stop working after about 2 weeks" (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/828937979095845728). Another forum thread describes "The Steam Offline Mode requires being re-logged in and validated on a regular basis (something like once every 30 days or so), you cant just set it offline and be good, it will eventualy fail and require re-authentication" (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/0/1700542332330146872). Current guides (2026) similarly state users can typically play "approximately 14 to 30 days before the client requires a re-authentication handshake" (https://gamewiki.blog/what-happens-if-i-play-steam-games-offline).

However, Valve's own official position directly contradicts the tweet's framing that this is Steam enforcing DRM by design. A Valve employee stated on the Steam forums: "This is not actually true - Offline Mode is designed to be indefinite... That said, there are many components involved in Offline Mode, and some of them have known issues and bugs which we are continually working to improve... It is not broken 'by design.'" and noted "The 'two week' timeout issue has been fixed for months now, along with several other bugs" (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/864969953572102601). This was also reported by Blue's News: "A response from Valve to a thread about offline mode on Steam indicates that the way offline mode currently requires users to go online periodically... is a bug, and not working as intended" (https://www.bluesnews.com/cgi-bin/board.pl?action=viewthread&boardid=1&threadid=146408).

Crucially, much of the real-world lockout behavior users experience is attributable to third-party DRM (especially Denuvo) layered onto specific games by publishers, not Steam's core platform. One forum user explained: "If you have games with Denuvo or other DRM, of launchers, they will ask to phone home every period (like 30 days)" (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/0/587308261888419215/). Another user directly addressed the 'Steam is secretly like Denuvo' argument: "There isn't any compulsory DRM in Steam. It's the publisher/developer's choice whether they want to implement it or not... it allows to play offline indefinitely and backup and reinstall your whole library at will while offline at all times" and added "All games using Valve's DRM allow offline play indefinitely since 2013" (https://steamcommunity.com/app/359870/discussions/0/1850323802590261402). A 2026 Notebookcheck report confirms Denuvo (third-party), not Steam, is tightening restrictions: "A hypervisor bypass developer discovered Denuvo now asks players to authenticate tokens online every 14 days" and "Many Steam games, besides NBA 2K26, already penalize offline players" due to Denuvo specifically (https://www.notebookcheck.net/Denuvo-bolsters-DRM-in-Steam-games-even-as-hypervisor-achieves-piracy-milestone.1283939.0.html).

Also, Valve's Steamworks DRM (when publishers opt in) is distinguishable from third-party DRM like Denuvo, and developers can use Steamworks services without enabling Steam's own DRM at all, undercutting the tweet's claim that Steam 'enforces their own DRM' universally.

In short: the empirical behavior many users observe (games failing after ~2-4 weeks offline) is real and documented, but it is predominantly driven by third-party DRM (Denuvo) that publishers choose to add, exactly as the quoted post states ('If a game has DRM, that is a developer/publisher decision'). Valve has stated Steam's own offline mode is designed/intended to be indefinite, contradicting the tweet's framing that Steam itself mandates a 30-day reauthentication that will inevitably break all games. The tweet overgeneralizes a real but inconsistent, largely third-party-DRM-driven phenomenon as an official, universal Steam-enforced 30-day DRM rule, which misrepresents the distinction the quoted post was making.

samples.research:
The tweet's core claim — that Steam enforces periodic re-authentication (unlike GOG's DRM-free installers that work forever) — has a kernel of truth, but the specific framing that Steam mandates re-login 'every 30 days' as a deliberate DRM policy is contradicted by Valve's own statements.

A Valve developer (Henry Goffin) directly addressed this on Steam's own forums, stating: 'This is not actually true - Offline Mode is designed to be indefinite. You can't access any of Steam's online features such as friends lists or saved game synchronization, of course, but the client should allow you to run in Offline Mode for as long as you like' (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/864969953572102601). He further clarified the commonly-cited timeout was a bug, not policy: 'The "two week" timeout issue has been fixed for months now, along with several other bugs' (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/864969953572102601).

This is corroborated by contemporaneous press coverage of the same Valve statement: PCGamesN reported '[it's] designed to be indefinite,' and that 'The "two week" timeout issue has been fixed for months now, along with several other bugs' (https://www.pcgamesn.com/steam-offline-mode-designed-be-indefinite-valve-are-working-make-it-more-robust). Kotaku reported the identical quote, '"Offline Mode is designed to be indefinite", writes Valve employee Henry Goffin on the company's forums' (https://kotaku.com/valve-is-constantly-trying-to-improve-steams-wonky-o-1458484605). CinemaBlend confirmed 'Goffin makes it clear that the offline mode's check-in is actually a bug... yes, it's a bug' (https://www.cinemablend.com/games/Steam-Offline-Mode-Was-Designed-Indefinite-Says-Valve-60311.html), and Blue's News also covered the statement that 'The "two week" timeout issue has been fixed for months now' (https://www.bluesnews.com/cgi-bin/board.pl?action=viewthread&boardid=1&threadid=146408). A later Steam forum post from a user named Satoru echoed this years afterward: 'there is a pervasive misconception that Offline Mode is designed to fail, phone home, requires reauthentication after X days, etc. this is not the case. Valves intended design for Offline Mode is it should be able to run permanently' (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/3043858334655604874/?l=spanish).

However, real-world user experience remains inconsistent even after Valve's fix. Various Steam community threads from different years describe forced re-authentication after roughly 30 days (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/0/1700542332330146872), while others report offline play lasting months with no limit (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/0/2798376078346605932). Current third-party guides from 2026 still disagree on the exact window: one cites a 'hidden' 30-day license-verification limit (https://gamewiki.blog/what-happens-if-i-play-steam-games-offline), another cites '2-3 weeks' (https://www.eneba.com/hub/games/game-guides/can-you-play-steam-offline/), and another says 7-10 days (https://theportablegamer.com/2026/03/25/how-to-go-offline-on-steam-complete-guide-to-invisible-mode-offline-play-in-2026/) — none of these cite an official Valve source for the number, and they contradict each other, suggesting these may be unreliable SEO content rather than verified current Valve policy.

Separately, certain specific games impose their own publisher-level DRM re-authentication windows (e.g., some Denuvo-protected games, or Diablo II: Resurrected's Battle.net-linked 30-day token) independent of Steam's own Offline Mode (https://steamcommunity.com/app/2536520/discussions/0/760680996704183750/, https://steamcommunity.com/app/584400/discussions/0/1474221865191573745/). This is a game/publisher-level DRM layer, distinct from the platform-level Steam Offline Mode the tweet describes, and may be the actual source of some '30 day' user anecdotes.

The tweet also conflates a temporary Steam server outage with Steam permanently shutting down forever — these have different implications for whether/when games would 'break.' GOG's claim that DRM-free installers work forever without any server check is uncontested. The quoted tweet's claim that Steam doesn't require game-level DRM (it's optional for publishers) is technically accurate but addresses a different layer than the original tweet's point about platform-level account authentication, so the two tweets largely talk past each other rather than one being flatly wrong.

Overall: Valve's official position (and press coverage corroborating it) is that Offline Mode is designed to be indefinite, with the common 'two week'/'30 day' timeout understood as a historical bug that was fixed. The tweet's specific '30 days' DRM-enforcement framing therefore appears to overstate and mischaracterize Steam's actual intended policy, even though anecdotal bugs/game-specific DRM can still sometimes force reauthentication in practice.

You can't access any of Steam's online features such as friends lists or saved game synchronization, of course, but the client should allow you to run in Offline Mode for as long as you like' (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/864969953572102601). He further clarified the commonly-cited timeout was a bug, not policy: 'The "two week" timeout issue has been fixed for months now, along with several other bugs' (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/864969953572102601).

This is corroborated by contemporaneous press coverage of the same Valve statement: PCGamesN reported '[it's] designed to be indefinite,' and that 'The "two week" timeout issue has been fixed for months now, along with several other bugs' (https://www.pcgamesn.com/steam-offline-mode-designed-be-indefinite-valve-are-working-make-it-more-robust). Kotaku reported the identical quote, '"Offline Mode is designed to be indefinite", writes Valve employee Henry Goffin on the company's forums' (https://kotaku.com/valve-is-constantly-trying-to-improve-steams-wonky-o-1458484605). CinemaBlend confirmed 'Goffin makes it clear that the offline mode's check-in is actually a bug... yes, it's a bug' (https://www.cinemablend.com/games/Steam-Offline-Mode-Was-Designed-Indefinite-Says-Valve-60311.html), and Blue's News also covered the statement that 'The "two week" timeout issue has been fixed for months now' (https://www.bluesnews.com/cgi-bin/board.pl?action=viewthread&boardid=1&threadid=146408). A later Steam forum post from a user named Satoru echoed this years afterward: 'there is a pervasive misconception that Offline Mode is designed to fail, phone home, requires reauthentication after X days, etc. this is not the case. Valves intended design for Offline Mode is it should be able to run permanently' (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/3043858334655604874/?l=spanish).

However, real-world user experience remains inconsistent even after Valve's fix. Various Steam community threads from different years describe forced re-authentication after roughly 30 days (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/0/1700542332330146872), while others report offline play lasting months with no limit (https://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/0/2798376078346605932). Current third-party guides from 2026 still disagree on the exact window: one cites a 'hidden' 30-day license-verification limit (https://gamewiki.blog/what-happens-if-i-play-steam-games-offline), another cites '2-3 weeks' (https://www.eneba.com/hub/games/game-guides/can-you-play-steam-offline/), and another says 7-10 days (https://theportablegamer.com/2026/03/25/how-to-go-offline-on-steam-complete-guide-to-invisible-mode-offline-play-in-2026/) — none of these cite an official Valve source for the number, and they contradict each other, suggesting these may be unreliable SEO content rather than verified current Valve policy.

This is a game/publisher-level DRM layer, distinct from the platform-level Steam Offline Mode the tweet describes, and may be the actual source of some '30 day' user anecdotes.

The tweet also conflates a temporary Steam server outage with Steam permanently shutting down forever — these have different implications for whether/when games would 'break.' GOG's claim that DRM-free installers work forever without any server check is uncontested. The quoted tweet's claim that Steam doesn't require game-level DRM (it's optional for publishers) is technically accurate but addresses a different layer than the original tweet's point about platform-level account authentication, so the two tweets largely talk past each other rather than one being flatly wrong.

# How to have reliable offline mode on Steam. :: Help and Tips

How to have reliable offline mode on Steam.

First off, I despise being forced to use Steam or indeed any other kind of invasive 3rd party middle man DRM, but since I have been gifted some free games and have also been stupid enough to pay for a few games that require Steam, I guess I am stuck with it, at least asd far as those games are concerned.

I work offshore. I am offshore for 5 weeks at a time. When I go offshore, I take my gaming laptop with me, which I like to play games on. Because I have no internet connection when I am offshore, I set all the invasive and defiling DRMs such as Origin and Steam to "OFFLINE MODE". Yet with Steam, even though I opt to log in in "OFFLINE MODE", after just a week or so, the Steam client tells me "There is no records of this username on your computer, please enter your username and password" With no internet connection, this is a pretty hard thing to do.

So my question is, if anyone would be so kind as to answer it, how do I make Steam go into a geniune offline mode, whereby I really don't need an internet connections to access my games.

I make no aopologies for the sour tone of my post. When Steam locked me out of my games that were meant to keep me amused for 5 weeks, rendering my gaming laptop an 8Kg weight around my neck, I was spitting bloody venom!

Since the client's launch back in 2004 users have come across bugs with the feature and being able to play your games without an internet connection has never been a guarantee. According to Goffin, the developer's been working on improvements that will go live "some day soon".

The comments spun out from [a thread](http://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/864969953572102601/) discussing the reliability of Steam's offline mode. MatTheCat complained that when he worked offshore for a five week stretch he'd find himself locked out from Steam, despite being in Offline Mode, and unable to access his game.

[User Facedown replied](http://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/864969953572102601/#c864969953589725150), saying "Off-line mode is designed to reset about every two weeks at which time you are supposed to go online again." This is what spurred Goffin to weigh in, [saying](http://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/864969953572102601/#c864969953730401285):

"This is not actually true - Offline Mode is designed to be indefinite. You can't access any of Steam's online features such as friends lists or saved game synchronization, of course, but the client should allow you to run in Offline Mode for as long as you like.

"That said, there are many components involved in Offline Mode, and some of them have known issues and bugs which we are continually working to improve. We're aware that it doesn't always work as flawlessly as we want it to, but please keep reporting bugs with Offline Mode. It is not broken 'by design'."

[Later in the thread](http://steamcommunity.com/discussions/forum/1/864969953572102601/#c864969953745925033) he adds that Valve "have been working very hard on upgrading the underlying technology in Steam. We have no community managers or PR people, so all the time that we spend on forums is taking away from development time. That said, I know that it's frustrating to get no response, and it looks like we aren't doing anything about it."

The good news from all this is that the developer is actually working on something that should substantially improve Offline Mode:

"Many of the older games on Steam were using an older authentication system which has many known issues with Offline Mode and is incredibly difficult to maintain - it was written for a time when there were dozens of games on Steam, not thousands," explains Goffin. "We are in the process of upgrading every game in the Steam catalog to a newer authentication system (and fixing bugs that result from the conversion), but this is a slow and time-consuming process. Some day soon, once this work is completed, we will eliminate the old authentication system (represented by the ClientRegistry.blob file) and Offline Mode should immediately become much more robust."

Of course, "some day soon" in Valve terms is difficult to quantify but the developer is at least aware of and working on the problem.

_Earlier this evening I wrote a similar version of this post but it took a much more antagonistic tone and presented the facts of this story as something they shouldn't have been. This version better reflects Goffin's comments._

# Options for dealing with your debts

[Skip contents](#guide-contents)

## Contents

1.  [Overview](/options-for-dealing-with-your-debts)
2.  Breathing Space (Debt Respite Scheme)
3.  [Debt Management Plans](/options-for-dealing-with-your-debts/debt-management-plans)
4.  [Administration orders](/options-for-dealing-with-your-debts/administration-orders)
5.  [Individual Voluntary Arrangements](/options-for-dealing-with-your-debts/individual-voluntary-arrangements)
6.  [Debt Relief Orders](/options-for-dealing-with-your-debts/debt-relief-orders)

## Breathing Space (Debt Respite Scheme)

If you live in England or Wales, you can get temporary protection from your creditors while you get debt advice and make a plan. This scheme is called ‘Breathing Space’.

You can get temporary protection for up to 60 days.

You’ll still need to make your debt repayments.

If you get it:

*   enforcement action cannot be taken against you
*   your creditors cannot contact you about debts included in your Breathing Space
*   your creditors cannot add interest or charges to your debt

If you’re getting mental health crisis treatment, your protection from creditors will be longer. It will last for the length of your treatment, plus another 30 days.

## How to apply for the Breathing Space scheme

To apply for the ‘Breathing Space’ scheme, you need to talk to a debt adviser. They will submit an application on your behalf if it’s the right thing to do.

You can [find a free debt adviser](https://www.moneyhelper.org.uk/en/money-troubles/dealing-with-debt/debt-advice-locator) on the MoneyHelper website. You can get confidential advice online, over the phone or in person.

If you’re receiving mental health treatment and cannot speak to a debt adviser, someone else can do so on your behalf.

## Costs

It’s free to apply for ‘Breathing Space’, but some debt advisers may charge you a fee.

## Eligibility

You must:

*   not have a debt relief order (DRO), an individual voluntary arrangement (IVA), an interim order, or be an undischarged bankrupt at the time you apply
*   not already be using the ‘Breathing Space’ scheme
*   not have used the ‘Breathing Space’ scheme in the last 12 months, unless it was for a mental health crisis

# Is There Debt Forgiveness in South Africa? - True North Debt

![](https://truenorthdebt.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Untitled-design-2025-03-05T114315.906-1280x488.jpg)

If you’re in a lot of debt and struggling to make repayments, you may have wondered whether there’s such a thing as [debt forgiveness](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/d/debt-relief.asp) in South Africa. Technically, there is: debt review, sequestration, **[reckless credit](https://truenorthdebt.co.za/reckless-lending-and-how-debt-review-can-help/reckless-lending/)** assessment, and prescription debt.

With rising economic pressures like inflation and the cost of living crisis, debt forgiveness has never been a more crucial measure. The National Credit Act has been paramount in debt forgiveness, creating a legal framework to relieve over-indebtedness with the introduction of debt review in 2005. The government recognised the hardships South Africans were facing as we became more credit-reliant in the wake of the early 2000s recession and economic depression.

This post discusses different means of debt forgiveness in South Africa, including debt review, sequestration, reckless credit assessment, and prescribing debt.

Let’s get into it.

## Debt Review

**[Debt review](https://truenorthdebt.co.za/how-debt-review-works/)** is a legal process wherein a debt counsellor negotiates on your behalf for lower interest rates and reduced repayments. Under debt review, you’re fully protected from legal action creditors might take, such as judgments or garnishee orders, unless you default on a payment or take out another loan. Debt review monthly payments are usually much lower than initial credit repayments, as creditors must agree to lower your repayments and interest rates to rescue you from over-indebtedness. The National Credit Act says:

Section 86 (5) says, “A consumer who applies to a debt counsellor, and each credit provider…must…comply with any reasonable requests by the debt counsellor to facilitate the  
evaluation of the consumer’s state of indebtedness and the prospects for  
responsible debt re-arrangement; and participate in good faith in the review and in any negotiations designed to result in responsible debt re-arrangement.”

Apply for debt review and get much lower interest rates and repayments, freeing up room in your budget for what’s important.

## Sequestration

Sequestration is another word for declaring bankruptcy. Under sequestration, your assets will be sold, so long as they cover at least 20% of your debt. The rest of your debt will be written off.

We don’t recommend this option, as sequestration can stay on your credit record for as long as 10 years. You’ll also lose valuable assets, such as your car or house.

## Reckless Credit

If someone lends you money without checking if you can afford it (conducting an affordability assessment) or disregards your inability to afford it, they have lent you money recklessly. Under the [National Credit Act (NCA)](https://barnardinc.co.za/understanding-the-national-credit-act-nca-for-your-business/), this is an illegal offence and can result in most or all of your debt being written off.

Debt counsellors can conduct reckless credit assessments, ensuring you don’t pay for debt that was recklessly lent to you.

## Prescription Debt

If neither you nor your creditor have been in contact for three years or more (depending on the type of debt), you can apply for the debt to be prescribed – **[written off](https://truenorthdebt.co.za/how-to-write-off-bad-debt/)**.

The prescription periods for debt are:

*   **3 years** for most unsecured debt (credit cards, personal loans, etc.)
*   **30 years** for home loans, judgments, and tax debt

After these periods have passed, it can no longer be collected. You can apply for the debt to be written off your credit report. Note that neither you nor your creditor must have made contact within that period. If you’ve made promises to pay the debt, or your creditor has contacted you regarding the debt, it can’t be prescribed.

![Is there debt forgiveness in South Africa? Learn about different debt forgiveness means, such as debt review, sequestration, prescription debt, and more!](https://truenorthdebt.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/2-13.jpg "Is there debt forgiveness in South Africa? Learn about different debt forgiveness means, such as debt review, sequestration, prescription debt, and more!")

## Let True North Debt Be of Assistance

During the debt review assessment process, we can assess for prescription debt and reckless credit. We’ll also negotiate for lower interest rates and repayments, ensuring you have extra room in your budget for what matters. To learn more, **[contact us](https://truenorthdebt.co.za/contact-us/)** today.

### Struggling to keep up with your debt?

You don’t have to face it alone. True North Debt’s registered debt counsellors can help you understand your options and take back control of your finances — starting with a free, no-obligation assessment.

# Is There Debt Forgiveness in South Africa? - True North Debt

![](https://truenorthdebt.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Untitled-design-2025-03-05T114315.906-1280x488.jpg)

If you’re in a lot of debt and struggling to make repayments, you may have wondered whether there’s such a thing as [debt forgiveness](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/d/debt-relief.asp) in South Africa. Technically, there is: debt review, sequestration, **[reckless credit](https://truenorthdebt.co.za/reckless-lending-and-how-debt-review-can-help/reckless-lending/)** assessment, and prescription debt.

With rising economic pressures like inflation and the cost of living crisis, debt forgiveness has never been a more crucial measure. The National Credit Act has been paramount in debt forgiveness, creating a legal framework to relieve over-indebtedness with the introduction of debt review in 2005. The government recognised the hardships South Africans were facing as we became more credit-reliant in the wake of the early 2000s recession and economic depression.

This post discusses different means of debt forgiveness in South Africa, including debt review, sequestration, reckless credit assessment, and prescribing debt.

Let’s get into it.

## Debt Review

**[Debt review](https://truenorthdebt.co.za/how-debt-review-works/)** is a legal process wherein a debt counsellor negotiates on your behalf for lower interest rates and reduced repayments. Under debt review, you’re fully protected from legal action creditors might take, such as judgments or garnishee orders, unless you default on a payment or take out another loan. Debt review monthly payments are usually much lower than initial credit repayments, as creditors must agree to lower your repayments and interest rates to rescue you from over-indebtedness. The National Credit Act says:

Section 86 (5) says, “A consumer who applies to a debt counsellor, and each credit provider…must…comply with any reasonable requests by the debt counsellor to facilitate the  
evaluation of the consumer’s state of indebtedness and the prospects for  
responsible debt re-arrangement; and participate in good faith in the review and in any negotiations designed to result in responsible debt re-arrangement.”

Apply for debt review and get much lower interest rates and repayments, freeing up room in your budget for what’s important.

## Sequestration

Sequestration is another word for declaring bankruptcy. Under sequestration, your assets will be sold, so long as they cover at least 20% of your debt. The rest of your debt will be written off.

We don’t recommend this option, as sequestration can stay on your credit record for as long as 10 years. You’ll also lose valuable assets, such as your car or house.

## Reckless Credit

If someone lends you money without checking if you can afford it (conducting an affordability assessment) or disregards your inability to afford it, they have lent you money recklessly. Under the [National Credit Act (NCA)](https://barnardinc.co.za/understanding-the-national-credit-act-nca-for-your-business/), this is an illegal offence and can result in most or all of your debt being written off.

Debt counsellors can conduct reckless credit assessments, ensuring you don’t pay for debt that was recklessly lent to you.

## Prescription Debt

If neither you nor your creditor have been in contact for three years or more (depending on the type of debt), you can apply for the debt to be prescribed – **[written off](https://truenorthdebt.co.za/how-to-write-off-bad-debt/)**.

The prescription periods for debt are:

*   **3 years** for most unsecured debt (credit cards, personal loans, etc.)
*   **30 years** for home loans, judgments, and tax debt

After these periods have passed, it can no longer be collected. You can apply for the debt to be written off your credit report. Note that neither you nor your creditor must have made contact within that period. If you’ve made promises to pay the debt, or your creditor has contacted you regarding the debt, it can’t be prescribed.

![Is there debt forgiveness in South Africa? Learn about different debt forgiveness means, such as debt review, sequestration, prescription debt, and more!](https://truenorthdebt.co.za/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/2-13.jpg "Is there debt forgiveness in South Africa? Learn about different debt forgiveness means, such as debt review, sequestration, prescription debt, and more!")

## Let True North Debt Be of Assistance

During the debt review assessment process, we can assess for prescription debt and reckless credit. We’ll also negotiate for lower interest rates and repayments, ensuring you have extra room in your budget for what matters. To learn more, **[contact us](https://truenorthdebt.co.za/contact-us/)** today.

### Struggling to keep up with your debt?

You don’t have to face it alone. True North Debt’s registered debt counsellors can help you understand your options and take back control of your finances — starting with a free, no-obligation assessment.
